title: Trading faith away harms only the trader.
subtitle: A bad bargain that Allah does not feel
then: Right after comforting the Prophet ﷺ about those rushing into disbelief, Allah describes people who {trap}bought disbelief at the price of faith.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says {idea}they will not harm Allah at all; they only harm themselves.{/idea}
now: You quietly trade your prayer time for overtime, your honesty for a better deal, your values to fit in with a new crowd. It feels like a small swap. {idea}Allah does not lose from it. You do.{/idea}
old: Giving up a bit of my faith is my business and costs no one.
new: When I trade faith away, I am the only one who pays.
try: Name one thing you have been trading your faith for. Take one step back from it today.

title: Getting away with it is not the same as being okay.
subtitle: When delay is not a sign of approval
then: Allah warns those who reject Him: {trap}do not think the delay in your punishment is good for you.{/trap} Ibn Kathir links it to verses about people given wealth and children who think it means Allah is pleased. {idea}The delay only lets the sin grow, unless they turn back.{/idea}
now: You cheated on the test and passed. You lied to your boss and nothing happened. Months go by and you start to think it was fine. {idea}The quiet is not a verdict. It is time given to repent.{/idea}
old: If nothing bad happened, it must not have been so bad.
new: Time without consequences is a chance to turn back, not proof I was right.
try: Think of one wrong you got away with. Ask Allah's forgiveness for it tonight.

title: Hard days sort the true from the pretending.
subtitle: Allah will not leave things mixed forever
then: Ibn Kathir says this refers to Uhud. {idea}Allah lets a calamity come so that His friend becomes known and His enemy exposed.{/idea} Believers showed patience and firmness; {trap}hypocrites showed their retreat.{/trap} People cannot see the unseen; Allah reveals it to whom He chooses of His messengers.
now: A crisis hits the family business, and you find out who stays to help and who disappears. It also shows you yourself. {idea}Hard days are a mirror.{/idea} The aim is not to judge others, but to see where you stand.
old: I already know who is real and who is not.
new: Trials reveal hearts, starting with mine, and the unseen belongs to Allah.
try: Ask yourself: in the last hard moment, how did I act? Write one honest line.

title: What you hold back will hang around your neck.
subtitle: Stinginess looks like gain, but it is loss
then: Ibn Kathir says the miser should not think piling up wealth helps him; {trap}it harms his religion and his worldly life.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ recited this verse about wealth whose zakah is not paid. {idea}And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth.{/idea}
now: Payday comes. You see the fundraiser link in the family chat and scroll past. You tell yourself you need a cushion. {trap}What you grip will not stay with you.{/trap} {idea}It all goes back to its Owner anyway.{/idea}
old: Keeping my money is what keeps me secure.
new: Everything returns to Allah; only what I give goes ahead of me.
try: Give a small amount today to someone in need, even if it feels inconvenient.

title: Allah heard them mock Him as poor.
subtitle: Every word is recorded
then: Ibn 'Abbas said when the verse about lending Allah a goodly loan came down, {trap}some in Madinah mocked: has your Lord become poor?{/trap} Allah replied that He heard them. {idea}He would record what they said{/idea}, along with the killing of prophets by their forebears.
now: A joke at the dinner table: why does God need my charity? Or a sarcastic comment under a fundraising post. {idea}Words about Allah are not small talk. They are written down.{/idea} The giving is for you, not for Him.
old: A sarcastic line about religion is just a joke.
new: Every word I say about Allah is heard and recorded, so I speak with care.
try: Next time religion comes up in a joke, stay quiet or change the subject kindly.

title: What your hands sent ahead is what you meet.
subtitle: Allah is never unjust to anyone
then: This closes the warning to those who mocked Allah and killed prophets. Ibn Kathir says it is said to them in rebuke: {trap}this is because of what your hands sent before you.{/trap} {idea}Allah is never unjust to His servants.{/idea}
now: Every message you send, every hour you spend, every coin you give or keep is going on ahead of you. {idea}You will meet it again.{/idea} The good news: you can send good ahead starting today.
old: What happens to me in the end is out of my hands.
new: My hands are sending things ahead each day, and Allah will treat me with perfect justice.
try: Send one good thing ahead today on purpose: a kind word, a gift, a prayer.

title: Proof was never really the problem.
subtitle: Demanding a sign you would ignore anyway
then: Some claimed Allah told them to believe no messenger until he brought an offering consumed by fire from the sky. {idea}Allah replied: messengers came before me with clear proofs, and with what you ask for.{/idea} {trap}So why did you kill them, if you are truthful?{/trap}
now: You say you will start praying once you feel it. Once you get a sign. Once your questions are all answered. {trap}Sometimes the demand for proof is a way to delay.{/trap} {idea}Ask yourself what would really change.{/idea}
old: I will commit once I get the right sign.
new: Often I already have enough; what I lack is the will to act.
try: Do one act of worship today you have been putting off until you feel ready.

title: If they deny you, they denied the best before you.
subtitle: Comfort for the rejected messenger ﷺ
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah comforts the Prophet ﷺ here: {idea}do not be sad that they deny you{/idea}, for messengers before you were denied too. {trap}They came with clear proofs, scriptures and an enlightening Book, and were still rejected.{/trap}
now: You shared something true and good, and people laughed, or unfollowed, or argued. You start to doubt yourself. {idea}Being rejected is not proof you were wrong.{/idea} The best people in history were rejected too.
old: If people reject what I say, I must be wrong.
new: Rejection happened to the messengers; it does not decide what is true.
try: Keep doing one good thing you do quietly, even though someone mocked it.

title: Every soul will taste death. Then the real pay.
subtitle: Who actually wins
then: Ibn Kathir says this verse comforts all creation: everyone dies, and only Allah remains. {idea}Full payment comes on the Day of Resurrection.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}a whip's length of space in Paradise is better than the world and all it holds.{/reward}
now: The promotion, the wedding photos, the new car, the number of followers. All of it feels like the scoreboard. {idea}The real scoreboard opens after the last breath.{/idea} Qatadah said: take obedience to Allah from this delight while you can.
old: Success means winning in this life.
new: Success is being kept from the Fire and let into Paradise; the rest passes.
try: Look at your plans for this week and add one thing that counts for the Hereafter.

title: You will be tested and you will hear hurtful words.
subtitle: Patience and taqwa are the strong choice
then: Early in Madinah, 'Abdullah bin Ubayy insulted the Prophet ﷺ when he came to a gathering and recited Quran. Sa'd bin 'Ubadah asked him ﷺ to pardon him, and {idea}he ﷺ forgave him.{/idea} The Companions used to {reward}bear the harm and forgive{/reward}, as this verse commanded.
now: The comment under your post. The relative who mocks your hijab or beard. The coworker's joke about your fasting. {trap}You will hear it.{/trap} {idea}Patience and mindfulness of Allah are not weakness. The verse calls them resolve.{/idea}
old: If I do not hit back, I look weak.
new: Patience with Allah in mind is the strongest response I have.
try: Next time someone says something hurtful, pause and say nothing for ten seconds.

title: They were trusted to share the truth and sold it cheap.
subtitle: Knowledge is meant to be made clear

row.title: share what helps
sub: it was given as a trust

then: Allah took a covenant from those given scripture to make it clear and not hide it. {trap}They threw it behind their backs for a small gain.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says this is {idea}a warning for every scholar not to do the same{/idea}, and to spread beneficial knowledge.
now: You know the truth in a family dispute but stay quiet because it is awkward. A friend asks you a question about the deen and you brush it off. {trap}Silence can be a small price too.{/trap} {idea}Share what you know, gently.{/idea}
old: What I know is mine to share or keep as I like.
new: Useful truth I know is a trust; I should make it clear, not sell it for comfort.
try: Share one beneficial thing you learned this week with someone who would benefit.

title: Loving praise for what you never did.
subtitle: A false image is no shelter

row.title: want praise
sub: for what they did not do

then: Ibn Kathir says this is about those who show off and claim deeds they did not do. Abu Sa'id said some hypocrites stayed back from battle, then {trap}swore excuses and wanted praise for what they did not do.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ said: {idea}one who claims what he was not given is like one wearing two robes of falsehood.{/idea}
now: The group project where you let people think the idea was yours. The photo that makes your charity look bigger than it was. The CV line stretched a little. {trap}The praise feels good.{/trap} {idea}It is a robe made of nothing.{/idea}
old: A little exaggeration about myself harms no one.
new: Praise for what I did not do is a costume that will not protect me.
try: Correct one place where people credit you for something you did not fully do.
